newsitem.title: USA: IRS targets 1990 Camden Cty authority for audit.
newsitem.headline: IRS targets 1990 Camden Cty authority for audit.

text.p: IRS is examining a six-year- old Camden County, N.J., tax-exempt bond offering to see if the bonds were properly designated as tax-exempt, a county authority recently announced.
The Camden County Municipal Utilities Authority disclosed the audit in a one-page notice filed on November 7 to electronic information repositories that report key events to the bond market.

"The Camden County Municipal Utilities Authority was notified by the Internal Revenue Service on May 8 that the Authority's ... Sewer Revenue Capital Appreciation Bonds Series 1990A and 1990B have been selected for examination," the notice says.
IRS is auditing the 1990 offerings, including a $115.8 million series and a $121.67 million series, under an expanded compliance program for tax-exempt bonds, the notice says.
"The Authority is cooperating with the Service," adds the notice.

"The Service has not to date challeng(ed) the tax-exempt status of the Bonds," the notice says. "The Authority is unable to predict when the Service will conclude its examination or what the outcome of the examination will be."
An attorney for the Camden authority said IRS has not told the authority why it is examining the bonds.
IRS does two kinds of tax-exempt bond audits - "random" and "targeted." The Camden County deals fall under the targeted category.
